issuing_body: Expert Group on How AI Principles Should be Implemented, Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
covered_actors: businesses using AI (BtoB and BtoC companies)

evidence.quote: The provision of guidelines that include desirable risk assessment and management is expected to facilitate deployment of AI.
Development/introduction of AI systems: Development of principles, creation of a management framework84, establishment of an escalation process, development of a risk management process85

This direction of improving consumer literacy is based on the assumption that companies, etc. using AI provide appropriate information to consumers. Therefore, an intermediate guideline to bridge the gap between AI Principles and corporate-level practice is deemed necessary in the sense of facilitating such information provision.

support the improvement of AI risk management, etc., function as a benchmark of trustworthiness of AI system in inter-company transactions, include useful good practices for companies that have just started using AI, and facilitate the provision of explanations to consumers, etc.
Operation of AI systems: Monitoring, internal audits, use of external evaluation, development of relationships with stakeholders, improvement and progress management

Further, in order to maintain public trust, utilize various forms of assurance depending on the risk, such as self-check, peer review, internal audit, agreed procedures, third-party review and external audit.

From the perspective of balancing respect for AI principles and promotion of innovation and at least at this moment, except for some specific areas, AI governance should be designed mainly with soft laws, which is favorable to companies that respect AI principles.
The above suggestions and notes point to non-binding intermediate goal-based guidelines to promote AI innovation and deployment.

implementation_notes: Non-binding expert group report (Ver. 1.1) analyzing domestic and international AI governance trends and proposing an ideal AI governance architecture for Japan. Recommends goal-based, risk-based governance centered on legally non-binding corporate governance guidelines and international standards (e.g., ISO/IEC JTC1 SC42), concludes that legally binding horizontal AI regulation is unnecessary in Japan at this time, favors existing sector-specific frameworks for areas such as automotive and healthcare, and outlines future issues including adoption incentives (e.g., government procurement points), guidance for government AI use, international harmonization, and monitoring and civil liability.
